name: Raise 2048 solver avg score (expspawn retrain, no eval-seed overfit)

description: Baseline: shipped 128/32 net (base TD, 300k) on new held-out seed 9200, 20 games, 2-ply.

asi.hypothesis: reference point, not a change
asi.note: seed 9200 is easier than 9000; use it for iteration only, confirm on 9300/9400

description: 1M-schedule base run: evaluated its ~210k checkpoint (lr still 0.0024), then annealed 70k more games at lr 0.0022. 2-ply stuck at ~76k with 0/20 8192 despite 1-ply recovering to 57.9k.

asi.cost: 1M run killed at ~210k after 52 min; anneal 70k = 926 s, 145.2M moves, 157k moves/s
asi.hypothesis: Stretching the built-in linear lr decay over 1M games would let more data pay off; a short late anneal from the mid-run checkpoint should recover the 300k-schedule quality.
asi.lesson: The 1M schedule keeps lr ~2x the 300k schedule at the same game count. A noisy V (high lr late) is usable for 1-ply greedy but poisons 2-ply max-over-second-moves: 1-ply 57.9k vs shipped 60.9k, but 2-ply 75.8k vs 134.9k. Annealing 70k from a noisy point does not fix the V ranking.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not stretch the decay; keep the shipped 300k schedule. Try train seed 2/3 at the same 300k recipe, and/or a faster-decay 400k run.
asi.result: 210k checkpoint at lr 0.0024 = 74.4k/10 games; +70k anneal to lr 2e-4 = 75.8k/20, 0/20 8192, 1-ply 57.9k. 2-ply did not recover.

description: Train seed 2 with the shipped 300k recipe (base, lr 0.003, par sqrt): diverged at 50,440/300,000 games

asi.cause: with train_games=300k the built-in decay gives lr 0.00255 at 50k, vs 0.00165 for the docs' 100k runs; seed 1 survives this, seed 2 does not
asi.failure: diverged at 50440/300000 games (non-finite or |w| > 1e6), not saving /tmp/base300k_s2c.bin; error: Diverged
asi.hypothesis: seed 2 at the shipped 300k schedule would give an independent sample of the same recipe
asi.lesson: the shipped 0.003 schedule sits at the stability edge; do not run seed 2 without a lower lr or a divergence guard
asi.next_action_hint: seed 3 only if a stable schedule is chosen; keep checkpoints

description: Train seed 1 300k at lr 0.002 (decay to 0.0002), evaluate the 250k checkpoint

asi.hypothesis: lr 0.002 for 300k would be more stable than 0.003 and give a better final V
asi.killed_at: 250000/300000 games by the 5400 s tool timeout
asi.lesson: lower lr undertrains at the same game budget; the shipped 0.003 schedule is better. This matches docs #135/#204 that game count and lr shape are already at the recipe's peak
asi.next_action_hint: do not lower the schedule lr to stabilize seeds; instead keep shipped lr and use checkpoints

description: SWA: average the last 4/8/16/32 checkpoints of a fresh 300k run and evaluate (best avg4 118,981.8)

asi.hypothesis: averaging nearby SGD checkpoints (SWA / Polyak averaging) smooths V and improves 2-ply ranking
asi.run: fresh 300k shipped-recipe run, killed at 285k; 57 unique checkpoints in /tmp/swa
asi.lesson: averaging raises 1-ply but destroys 2-ply, same signature as low-lr fine-tuning: the averaged V stops being the search-compatible value. SWA over 20k+ games is a dead end
asi.reproducibility: fresh 300k run does NOT reproduce shipped (116.9k at 285k vs 134.9k); nn.zig changed since the 2026-11-06 shipped net (#289/#321/#348), so each long run is a fresh sample with ~±6-8k variance; shipped may be a high draw
asi.caution: 4-point SWA sweep is a single run, not a controlled A/B
asi.next_action_hint: do not pursue checkpoint averaging; treat 134.9k as a high-variance target and require fresh-seed confirmation

description: phase_h6: full-width 3-ply only in the low-empty endgame (2-ply at >=4 empties). Seed 9200 +12.6k (147,442.8, 18/20 8192) looked strong, but seed 9300 paired diff was +10,801.8 +/- 10,050.1 and seed 9400 unpaired was +747.6 (134,452.8 vs 133,705.2, 8192 15/20 vs 16/20). No reliable score gain at 4.0-4.7x ms/move; 20-game seed noise is ~+/-10k.

asi.bugs_found: Phase.max_empty default must be 16 (empty 4x4 board); 15 caused an unreachable in phaseDepth for the .deep schedule. min_empty=3 alone also matches 4+ empties, so an 'exactly 3' row needs an upper bound.
asi.cost: 4.11 ms/move at 9200, 4.73 at 9400, 15.04 in the serial pairrow process; 3,852-3,935 leaves/move vs 980-986 for 2-ply
asi.dead_ends: 3-ply only at <=2 empties: 127,852.2 (-7k, 2.15x); sampled 2 spawns in the 3-ply tree: 60,533 (-74k, policy collapses); 3-ply only at exactly 3 empties: 4.29x cost, 119,384.8 on 5 games (the 3-empty root tree dominates cost).
asi.hypothesis: 3-ply expectimax restricted to <=3 empty cells buys the 8192 tail cheaply (between the shipped 2-ply and the 12.7x full 3-ply).
asi.next_action_hint: Stop tuning endgame depth; it is a cost curve, not a free win. If depth is revisited, add a min_max_tile condition so only 4096+ tail boards pay for 3-ply, and confirm with pairrow on 2 seeds.
asi.noise_floor: 20 games on one seed: ~+/-10k; identical recipe reruns at 300k differ by ~+/-8k (fresh 285k run = 116,965.8 vs shipped 134,867.2).
asi.why_rejected: The gain does not replicate on a third seed and is under 1.1 sigma on the paired seed; at 4x ms/move it fails the +20% latency budget and is not a real score improvement.

description: expspawn 40k with a 40k lr schedule, par + batch_scale 1.0: 37,552.4 avg2ply (13,447.6 1-ply, 0/20 8192), 1.30 ms/move. Far below the shipped 134,867.2 and below the documented serial 20k expspawn (61.6k); par+bs1 is 8x undertrained, so this does not refute expspawn, but it is unusable as run.

asi.hypothesis: expspawn (expected-spawn TD(0)) at 40k games with a 40k schedule reproduces the documented 20k win (61.6k vs base 30.7k) and scales toward the shipped net.
asi.measurement: 40,000 games, 21,457,408 moves in 1,033.7 s (20.8k moves/s) via par + batch_scale 1.0; final net 37,552.4 avg2ply, 13,447.6 avg1ply, 0/20 8192.
asi.why_it_failed: par + batch_scale 1.0 takes 8x fewer steps than serial (one merged step per 8 games with no scaling), so 40k games is only ~5k serial-equivalent games of training. The documented 20k expspawn run was serial (2,890 s, 5,977 moves/s), not par.
asi.prior_run: 300k expspawn at par bs1 ran 60k games in 22 min (~5 h total) and its 50k checkpoint (lr 0.00085) scored 44,141.8 / 1-ply 15,133.6; killed.
asi.next_action_hint: Only retry expspawn with the guard relaxed to allow par + batch_scale sqrt(8) (the base recipe's rule), so 40k games carry real update magnitude; compare against a base 40k run on the same eval. Without that, expspawn needs serial training, which is ~1.7 h per 40k games here.
asi.lesson: batch_scale is a step-size knob, not part of the target definition: the guard that rejects non-1 batch_scale forces either 8x undertraining (par bs1) or serial speed.
asi.noise_floor: 20 games on one seed ~+/-10k; 37.5k vs 61.6k is far outside that, so this is a real undertraining failure, not noise.

description: expspawn 40k, lr 0.001 with a 40k schedule, par + batch_scale sqrt(8) (guard relaxed to allow it): 46,458.8 avg2ply, 14,896.4 1-ply, 0.99 ms/move, +38% over base 40k (33,647.2). Still far below 134,867.2; establishes the budget slope for a 300k run.

asi.cost: 30,750,277 moves in 1,297.8 s (23.7k moves/s) via par + batch_scale sqrt(8)
asi.guard_change: expectedSpawnIsPlainTd1 now copies opts.batch_scale into the comparison, so par + sqrt(8) is accepted; everything else stays default.
asi.hypothesis: expspawn at 40k with par + batch_scale sqrt(8) (rather than 1.0) carries enough update magnitude to show the documented 2x edge over base.
asi.next_action_hint: Scale to 300k with par + sqrt(8) (about 1.8 h): 40k*2.83 = 106k serial-equivalent steps, still 2.83x under the shipped 300k, but expspawn's sample efficiency may close the gap. bs 8 (linear) is the exact match but risks the divergence seen at lr 0.003.
asi.result: +38% over base at the same budget (46,458.8 vs 33,647.2), but still 3x below the shipped 134,867.2 - consistent with the budget being far too small, not with a broken method.
asi.why_not_kept: Primary metric far below the shipped net; this run only establishes the training slope.

description: expspawn 300k at lr 0.001, par + batch_scale sqrt(8), killed at 190,000 games: 92,377.0 avg2ply, 43,855.8 1-ply, 5/20 8192, 1.92 ms/move. Trajectory 40k 46.5k -> 85k 75.3k -> 190k 92.4k; behind the current base recipe (~103k at 190k) and far below shipped 134,867.2, so not a candidate.

asi.hypothesis: expspawn scaled to 300k games with par + batch_scale sqrt(8) (106k serial-equivalent steps) closes the 40k-to-300k gap and beats the shipped 134,867.2.
asi.why_stopped: At 190k expspawn is already behind the current base recipe at the same budget (base 100k=82.6k, 300k=113.7k, so ~103k at 190k) and 42k short of the shipped net with only 110k games plus the final anneal left; the earlier +38% edge over base at 40k has inverted.
asi.cost: 190k games in ~3.2 h (~800 games/min, ~500 moves/game after 100k)
asi.next_action_hint: expspawn is closed for this machine: serial is 1.7 h per 40k games, par+bs1 is 8x undertrained, par+sqrt(8) scales worse than base after ~100k. Characterize the base recipe's seed-to-seed variance instead (seed 2 at lr 0.0028 to survive the 0.003 divergence; 300k base is only ~18 min).
asi.lesson: The Rao-Blackwellized target helps at small budgets (lower variance) but its bias/flatness hurts late: 1-ply 43.9k at 190k vs the base recipe's much sharper V, and 2-ply tracks the base at best.

description: Control: base 128/32, 300k games, lr 0.003, seed 1, par with the documented batch_scale sqrt(8)=2.8284271247461903: 108,899.0 avg2ply, 60,502.8 1-ply, 9/20 8192, 1.03 ms/move. Matches the shipped net's 1-ply but is 26k short at 2-ply; the shipped 134,867.2 is still not reproduced.

asi.control: Same recipe at batch_scale 1.0 (the `-` default) reached 116,965.8 at 285k on seed 9200 and 76.6k for seed 2 - so batch_scale 1.0 is not the sole explanation of the gap; the shipped net is ~20k above every rerun.
asi.hypothesis: The earlier reruns were 8x undertrained because `-` in the batch_scale slot means 1.0, not sqrt(8); rerunning the documented recipe with 2.8284271247461903 at 300k should reproduce the shipped net.
asi.next_action_hint: Rerun the recipe at the commit that last changed ai/solver/nn_weights.bin (#233, 2026-11-06) in a worktree; if that reproduces ~135k on seed 9200, the current training path regressed (or the old net is simply a high draw) and the old code is the base to improve from.
asi.result: 108,899.0 (1-ply 60,502.8 - now equal to the shipped 60,864.6 - and 9/20 8192 vs 15/20). The 1-ply parity with a 26k 2-ply deficit isolates the gap to the *deep* tail, not general V quality.
asi.runs: 300k total: 225k foreground (killed by the 2400 s tool timeout), then resume 75k at lr 0.001 decaying to 0.0001 (1,179 s).

description: Verification: retrained the shipped recipe from scratch (128/32, base, 300k games, lr 0.003, seed 1, par, batch_scale 2.8284271247461903) and got weights bit-identical to ai/solver/nn_weights.bin (sha256 match), hence the same 134,867.2. The training path is deterministic; earlier reproducibility/variance conclusions were caused by batch_scale 1.0 (`-`) runs being 8x undertrained.

asi.finding: The shipped 300k recipe is bit-for-bit deterministic on this machine: training seed 1 with base, lr 0.003, par, batch_scale sqrt(8) for 300k games reproduces ai/solver/nn_weights.bin exactly (sha256 c98ea27c...).
asi.invalidated: Earlier conclusions that the shipped net is an unreproducible high draw, and that 300k runs vary +/-8k, were artifacts of running `par - -` (batch_scale 1.0, 8x undertrained) or of resume/anneal splits. The 285k bs1 run (116.9k), the 40k base (33.6k), the seed-2 300k bs1 (76.6k) and the SWA experiment are all under-trained controls, not evidence about variance.
asi.lesson: `-` in the batch_scale slot means 1.0, not sqrt(batch): `parseBatchScale` returns 1.0 for `-`, and only args[12] can set 2.8284271247461903. Every par run must pass the value explicitly.
asi.next_action_hint: With a deterministic baseline, re-test the endgame 3-ply (h6) paired on seed 9000: re-add the phase_h6 mode (it was reverted in log #6), then pairrow A=row2 B=row28, 20 games. Only adopt if mean diff - 2*stderr > 0 and the 8192 count rises.
asi.verification: Eval on seed 9200 with the reproduced weights: 134,867.2, 1-ply 60,864.6, 15/20 8192, 5,716.2 moves, 0.98 ms/move - identical to the shipped-net baseline.

description: Endgame 3-ply (phase_h6) re-test with a paired run on the docs' seed 9000: A (2-ply) 141,548.0 vs B 144,256.0, mean diff +2,708.0 +/- 8,531.5 (10W/10L), 8192 18/20 vs 17/20, 3.9x leaves and 4x ms/move. Combined with 9200 +12.6k, 9300 +10.8k +/- 10.1k, 9400 +0.7k: no reliable gain, so the mode is reverted.

asi.conclusion: Endgame 3-ply is a wash: no seed shows a significant gain, and the cost is 4x ms/move. Search depth is closed unless the tree itself gets cheaper.
asi.cost: leaves/move 3,880.5 vs 952.3; 14.82 vs 3.67 ms/move in the serial pairrow process
asi.why_rejected: Only the 9200 unpaired run cleared the noise; two paired runs are within 0.3 sigma of zero and h6 even loses a 8192 game on 9000. At 4x latency it cannot be adopted.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not revisit phase depth without a cheaper tree (node TT associativity, a smaller leaf net) or a risk/tile condition that limits it to 4096+ boards. The V recipe is deterministic and already at its peak; the session has no measured lever above 134,867.2.

description: Enlarge the native node-TT from 4096 to 16384 entries in ai/solver/nn.zig: on the 3-ply row the score is bit-identical (146,470.7) while leaves drop 6.5% and ms/move 4.9%; the default 2-ply benchmark is unchanged at 134,867.2.

asi.hypothesis: A larger direct-mapped node cache raises the 3-ply hit rate and cuts leaf work at identical results.
asi.log_note: The cache is a deterministic memo; the score cannot change, only leaves/time.
asi.measured: Row 15 (3-ply with node TT default) 3 games seed 9200: score 146,470.7 both, leaves 10,251.5 -> 9,581.2 per move (-6.5%), ms/move 17.42 -> 16.57 (-4.9%), hit_rate 17.8%.
asi.next_action_hint: A 4-way associative 16k table (4k buckets x 4 ways) should raise the hit rate further; only pursue if the goal becomes shipping 3-ply.
asi.score_unchanged: Official benchmark after the change: avg2ply 134,867.2, 1-ply 60,864.6, 15/20 8192, 954.9 leaves/move, 1.00 ms/move - the 2-ply path never touches the node TT, so the primary metric is untouched.
asi.why_keep: No primary regression and a strict efficiency win on the opt-in 3-ply row; 768 KiB per thread native, wasm capacity unchanged at 1<<9.

description: Tile-gated endgame 3-ply (phase_h5: 2-ply until 4096, then 3-ply at <=3 empties) scores 119,494.6 on seed 9200 with 12/20 8192 at 3.22 ms/move - worse than both the 2-ply baseline and the ungated h6. The mid-game depth switch itself costs the gain.

asi.conclusion: Conditioning the endgame depth on progress backfires: 119,494.6 and 12/20 8192, far worse than both the ungated h6 (147,442.8 on this seed) and the 2-ply baseline (134,867.2).
asi.cost: 3.22 ms/move, 3,008.3 leaves/move, node hit 15.1% - between 2-ply and h6, as expected, but the score paid for it.
asi.hypothesis: Gate the endgame 3-ply on a 4096+ board so the 8192 conversion depth is paid for only where it can matter.
asi.mechanism: A phase row can now require progress (min_max_tile) via core.maxTile, so boards under 4096 keep 2-ply. The switch mid-game is the suspect: the 2-ply prefix steers to boards whose 3-ply value differs, and the search horizon discontinuity undoes the gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not gate depth on tile progress. If 3-ply is ever revisited it must apply consistently from the start (h6) and the cost has to come from the tree, not from pretence.
asi.side_effect: 2/20 games died below 2048, consistent with the 2-ply/3-ply inconsistency.
asi.why_rejected: 20 games seed 9200: avg 119,494.6 vs 134,867.2 baseline, 8192 12/20 vs 15/20, and below the ungated h6 147,442.8. No seed needed; the regression is far outside the noise.

description: 4-way set-associative node TT (16384 entries, 4096 buckets, shallowest-first eviction) on the 3-ply row: identical score 146,470.7 but 16.67 vs 16.57 ms/move and a lower hit rate (16.6% vs 17.8%). No win; direct-mapped 16k stays.

asi.conclusion: Set-associativity buys nothing here: with the same total capacity the 4-way table is 0.6% slower than direct-mapped and its hit rate is lower (16.6% vs 17.8%). The depth-based eviction displaces deep nodes for shallow ones.
asi.hypothesis: Collisions, not capacity, limit the node TT; 4 ways per bucket should raise the 17.8% hit rate.
asi.measured: Row 15, 3 games seed 9200: score 146,470.7 identical, leaves 9,465.0/move (vs 9,581.2 direct 16k), 16.67 vs 16.57 ms/move, hit_rate 16.6% vs 17.8%.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the direct-mapped 16384-entry table (commit ef6d986). Do not spend more on the TT: the 3-ply cost is tree-bound, not cache-bound; h6 stays ~4x and is not adoptable under the +20% ms/move rule.
asi.why_rejected: Slightly slower, lower hit rate, identical score; the shallowest-first eviction is the likely regression.

description: 400k-game straight linear decay (0.003 -> 0.0003) from scratch, seed 1, par sqrt: 85,445.2 on seed 9200 (3/20 8192) vs 134,867.2 for the 300k shipped recipe. Stretching the schedule spends the low-lr tail over too many games; the anneal must be the last ~10% in absolute terms.

asi.conclusion: Stretching the shipped schedule over more games fails badly (-49k): the net needs the final low-lr tail in absolute terms, not proportionally. This reproduces the 1M failure and docs #204 schedule C with a clean deterministic run.
asi.final_lr: 0.0003 at 400k, but only the last 10% (40k games) of the run is below 0.0003, so the net never settles.
asi.hypothesis: More self-play games with the same linear-to-10% decay shape (400k, lr 0.003 -> 0.0003) buys more experience at the endgame without losing the anneal.
asi.measured: 20 games seed 9200: avg2ply 85,445.2 (3/20 8192, 1,110.2 leaves/move, 1.22 ms/move) vs 134,867.2 for the 300k net.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not stretch the schedule. A longer run only helps if the low-lr tail is extended in absolute games (e.g. 300k then 30k at 0.0003 fixed) - but #135's resume at lr 0.0001 lost 8%, so the evidence says no.
asi.runtime: 400k games, 696,423,075 moves in 4,375.9 s; checkpoints every 5k in /tmp/base400k.bin.
asi.why_rejected: The result is worse than the baseline by a factor the eval cannot explain: 85.4k vs 134.9k, 8192 3/20 vs 15/20, and 1-ply 49.1k vs 60.9k. A genuinely hotter, less settled net.

description: 300k games at lr 0.0028 (shipped shape, seed 1, par sqrt): 113,191.8 on seed 9200 (10/20 8192) vs 134,867.2 at 0.003. The shipped lr is the measured optimum of the sweep 0.002 / 0.0028 / 0.003.

asi.conclusion: The shipped lr is a measured peak, not just a stability edge: 0.0028 completes cleanly (no divergence) yet lands 21.7k below 0.003.
asi.hypothesis: lr 0.0028 avoids the 0.003 divergence edge while keeping the shipped schedule's shape, so it might match or beat 134,867.2.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not sweep lr downward again; 0.003 is the peak. Upward is blocked by seed-2 divergence at 0.003. The recipe has no free parameter left.
asi.runtime: 300k games, 544,169,801 moves in 3,544.0 s, no divergence.

description: Third train seed at the shipped 300k recipe (lr 0.003, par sqrt): collapses to 1,160 moves/game and 23,119.2 on seed 9200 (0/20 8192), after seed 2 diverged at 50k. The 0.003 recipe succeeds on roughly one seed in three; the shipped net is a high draw, not a reproducible level.

asi.conclusion: The 0.003/300k recipe is a lottery, not a stable recipe: seed 1 is the shipped 134,867.2 net, seed 2 diverges at 50,440 games, seed 3 collapses to a 1,160-move policy that never reaches 4096. The shipped net is a high draw.
asi.hypothesis: A third train seed at the shipped recipe gives a second strong net for an ensemble and measures the seed spread at 300k.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not retrain at 0.003 expecting the shipped level: 1 of 3 seeds reached it. If a retrain is ever needed, budget 3-4 seeds and select by a policy-quality gate (moves/game, 4096 reach) before spending evals - never by the benchmark score.
asi.seed_spread_300k: seed 1 134,867.2 (stable), seed 2 divergence at 50,440, seed 3 collapse (1,160 moves/game, 23,119.2).
asi.why_rejected: Far below baseline and structurally broken (no 4096 in 20 games); also removes the 2-net ensemble option because no second strong net exists.

description: replay_k=0 vs 30 at 300k/seed 1: weights come out byte-identical to the shipped net, proving the base variant has no replay phase and the CLI's replay_k slot is inert for it. The recipe's only active knobs are games, lr, seed and par batch_scale, all already pinned.

asi.conclusion: Base has no replay phase at all: `buildBase` returns `.{}`, so CLI arg 7 (replay_k) is inert for variant base. The docs' `base 30` command line convention is a positional placeholder, not a recipe knob. The shipped recipe is fully determined by (games, lr, train seed, par batch_scale); there is nothing else left to tune in it.
asi.hypothesis: replay_k (the afterstate re-training count at 0.5 lr) is a real recipe knob; dropping it might remove a late-training drag and beat the shipped net at the same seed.
asi.measured: replay_k=0, 300k, lr 0.003, seed 1, par sqrt, 553,202,634 moves in 3,723.8 s: weights sha256 c98ea27cf723cc96258173bd7be74630e80c2f1f358777c5ddaec059ec19a6c1, byte-identical to ai/solver/nn_weights.bin; eval 134,867.2 / 60,864.6 / 15-20 / 5,716.2 moves / 1.03 ms/move.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop sweeping CLI knobs: games, lr, seed, par are the only active inputs and all are pinned by measurement. The remaining levers are architectural (V architecture, target, search), each needing a fresh full retrain and multi-seed gating.
asi.why_rejected: No change at all - identical weights, so the experiment cannot improve the metric.

description: 30k-game resume of the shipped net at constant lr 0.0003 (+547 s training, no architecture/schedule change): 144,437.4 on seed 9200 (+7.1%, 18/20 8192), 136,147.2 on 9000 (+19.8%), 129,883.8 on 9300 (+3.6%), 135,032.0 on 40 games seed 9000 (+11.1%). +4% ms/move. Adopted as the shipped net with re-recorded golden tests, regenerated f32 twin and a history entry.

asi.conclusion: A 30k-game resume of the shipped net at the final lr (0.0003, constant) is a real score jump on every held-out seed tested: +9,570 (9200), +22,465 (9000), +4,562 (9300), and +13,463 on the docs' 40-game seed-9000 benchmark (34/40 vs 25/40 8192). Cost +4% ms/move. Adopted: weights, f32 twin, golden tests, docs entry.
asi.hypothesis: The shipped net is under-annealed at its 300k endpoint: the built-in decay ends at lr 0.0003 but stops after one pass, so 30k more games at that same rate can polish the tail without the lr ramp that failed at 100k.
asi.next_action_hint: The polish recipe is not yet reproducible: the same 30k/3e-4 on train seed 4 gave 134,058.2 (-809, neutral), so the gain belongs to the seed-1 trajectory. Next candidates if continues: sweep polish length (15k/60k) from the shipped net, and check whether polishing twice compounds. Do not tune the polish length on seed 9200 alone - confirm on 9000/9300.
asi.residual_risk: Selection was made with the 9200 benchmark visible, but the net also wins on two seeds measured afterwards, by +19.8% and +3.6%. Single-game golden seed 20240601 got worse for nn2 (132,164 -> 80,248) and better for nn (81,104 -> 112,940), a reminder of per-game variance.

description: Polish-length check: 15k at lr 3e-4 led the 30k net on the two selection seeds (9000 +10,989, 9300 +1,140) but lost on the two held-out seeds (9200 -9,482, 9400 -13,404). Four-seed aggregate 30k wins; the 20-game per-seed ranking is noise.

asi.conclusion: The 15k polish looked +12.1k better than 30k on the two seeds used for selection (9000, 9300) and then lost on both seeds not used (-9,482 on 9200, -13,404 on 9400). Aggregate over four 20-game seeds: 30k 545,257.4 vs 15k 534,500.6. Per-seed 20-game comparisons cannot rank nets; the 30k net stays.
asi.hypothesis: Polish length 15k beats 30k (it led on seed 9000 by +10,989 and on 9300 by +1,140), so the optimum is shorter than 30k.
asi.lesson: Selection on 2 seeds with 20 games each is a trap: signs flip on the seeds held out. Use at least 4 seeds (80 games) or 40 games per seed before switching weights.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the shipped 30k net. Do not run more polish-length points at 20 games per seed; if the length must be settled, use 40+ games on 4 seeds (about 1.5 h per point). A 60k continuation (seed-2, 547 s) was trained but is confounded by the seed change and was not evaluated.
asi.why_rejected: Lower benchmark and lower four-seed aggregate than the shipped 30k net.

description: Second 30k polish pass (60k total at constant lr 3e-4, 566 s): benchmark 150,747.2 (+11.8% over the 30k net), and the four-seed aggregate 584,697.0 vs 545,257.4 (+7.2%) with 3 of 4 seeds up (8192 69/80). Adopted; goldens, f32 twin and history updated.

asi.conclusion: A second 30k polish pass (60k total at lr 3e-4) improves the four-seed aggregate by +39,440 (+7.2%) with 3 of 4 seeds up; adopted as the new shipped net (150,747.2 on the benchmark). Polishing is still paying at 60k, with seed 9000 flat, so the curve is near but not past saturation.
asi.hypothesis: The 30k polish was not a one-off: continuing the same constant-lr resume for another 30k games (60k total from the base net) pushes the four-seed aggregate past the 30k net.
asi.next_action_hint: Adopted. The natural continuation is a third 30k pass (90k total) judged on the same four seeds, pre-registered rule: keep only if the aggregate beats 584,697.0 and at least 3 of 4 seeds are >= the 60k values. Stop the series when two points in a row flatten.
asi.seed_9000_flat: The only non-improving seed; watch whether the next pass turns it negative, which would mark the end of the polish series.

description: Third 30k polish pass (90k total): four-seed aggregate falls 584,697.0 -> 578,302.6 (9000 +5,135, 9200 -3,347, 9300 +1,525, 9400 -9,707). Polish saturates at 60k; the shipped 60k net stays.

asi.conclusion: The polish series has saturated at 60k. A third 30k pass (90k total) drops the four-seed aggregate by 6,394 (578,302.6 vs 584,697.0): seed 9000 rises +5,135, 9300 +1,525, but 9200 falls -3,347 and 9400 -9,707. 60k stays shipped; the pre-registered stop rule fires.
asi.hypothesis: A third 30k polish pass keeps improving the four-seed aggregate (the 0k->30k->60k curve was still rising).
asi.next_action_hint: Polish is closed: 60k is the peak of the three points (agg 545,257 -> 584,697 -> 578,303). Further constant-lr polishing will trade seeds against each other. Remaining directions are new mechanisms, not more polish: a second sequential series at a lower lr (e.g. 1e-4) as an anneal tail, or the search/V structural work already closed.
asi.why_rejected: Lower four-seed aggregate and only 2 of 4 seeds non-worse, so the pre-registered rule rejects it.

description: Anneal tail of 10k games at lr 1e-4 after the 60k polish: four-seed sum +6,504 but 9200 -8,287 and 9300 -3,598 (2/4 seeds non-worse), so the rule rejects it. Seed-trading, not an improvement; the 60k net stays.

asi.conclusion: A 10k-anneal tail at lr 1e-4 lifts the four-seed sum by 6,504 but trades the benchmark away: 9200 -8,287 (-5.5%), 9300 -3,598 (-2.5%), 9000 +17,317, 9400 +1,072 (2 of 4 seeds non-worse). Fails both the pre-registered 3-of-4 rule and the docs' 3% band on two seeds, so the 60k net stays.
asi.hypothesis: A short low-lr tail (10k games at 1e-4) after the 60k polish settles the weights and improves the aggregate without the seed-trading of the 90k pass.
asi.lesson: Seed-trading shows up as a positive aggregate with a negative benchmark. Judge on the per-seed band, not just the sum: 9200 and 9300 both fell by more than the 3% band while 9000 jumped +17k.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add lr-schedule tails on top of the polish: every extra pass trades seeds. The remaining honest options are structural (V architecture / target / search), each needing a full retrain, and none has a prior above noise in this repo's history.
asi.why_rejected: Only 2 of 4 seeds non-worse and the benchmark -5.5%, outside the docs' 3% band; the aggregate gain is seed-trading.

description: Out-of-sample check on seeds 9500/9600 (never used for any decision): the shipped 60k net scores 155,944.2 and 151,678.0 vs 118,945.0 and 122,604.4 for the pre-polish net (+31%/+24%, 8192 19/20 vs 12/20 and 14/20). The polish gain generalizes to unseen seeds; six-seed mean 124.9k to 148.7k.

asi.conclusion: Out-of-sample confirmation: the polish gain is not seed selection. On 9500/9600 (never used for any decision) the 60k net beats the pre-polish 300k net by +31.1% and +23.7% with 19/20 8192 on both, versus 12/20 and 14/20. Six-seed mean 124.9k -> 148.7k (+19%).
asi.hypothesis: The shipped 60k net's gain was selected on seeds 9000-9400, so a fresh pair of seeds could show it is overfit; testing 9500/9600 with the same eval code measures that directly.
asi.next_action_hint: The net is confirmed; the benchmark number 150,747.2 is conservative relative to the six-seed mean (148,700). Any future change must beat this net on the six seeds, not on 9200 alone.
asi.verification: No code or weights changed; docs and prompt record the check (commit 3721966).

description: 60k polish through a different train seed (seed 2): four-seed sum 609,407 vs 584,697 (+4.2%) and benchmark 155,704.2 (+3.3%), but 1-ply falls 64,201 -> 54,694 with 2/20 games dead below 2048. Gain is ~1.5 sigma; the balance favors the shipped seed-1 net.

asi.conclusion: The polish mechanism generalizes across RNG trajectories (a seed-2 polish lands at 609,407 vs 584,697 on four seeds), but the seed-2 net buys +4.2% 2-ply by giving up 15% at 1-ply (54,694 vs 64,201, 2/20 dead below 2048). The 2-ply edge is ~1.5 sigma on 80 games, the 1-ply loss is larger and consistent, so the seed-1 60k net stays shipped.
asi.hypothesis: A 60k polish reached through a different train seed (seed 2) is better than the shipped seed-1 polish, and proves the mechanism is not trajectory-specific.
asi.next_action_hint: If 1-ply is ever confirmed irrelevant to the product, this net is the strongest 2-ply artifact measured (609,407). Before switching on 1-ply grounds, check the app's fallback path and README: nn2 is the product policy, 1-ply is a diagnostic.
asi.trade_off: 2-ply +4.2% aggregate (+3.3% benchmark) vs 1-ply -15% and 2/20 dead games.
asi.why_rejected: The 2-ply gain is inside the +/-4% seed variance band (about 1.5 sigma on 80 games) while the 1-ply regression is larger and consistent; shipping it would trade a diagnostic metric for a statistical coin flip.

description: User-visible metadata fix: policy_info advertised the pre-polish net (nn2 121,569, nn 69,717, nn3 137,342). Re-measured on the documented protocol with the shipped net: nn 71,742 (40 games), nn2 141,292 (40 games, 34/40 8192), nn3 157,429 (20 games, 19/20). Primary metric unchanged by design.

asi.conclusion: The shipped net is now honestly labelled. The picker claims nn2 141,292 (40 games seed 9000, 34/40 8192) instead of the stale 121,569, nn 71,742 and nn3 157,429 (20 games). No score path changed; the benchmark is identical to run #22.
asi.hypothesis: policy_info's score strings were measured on the pre-polish net and are now user-visible lies: nn2 advertises 121,569 while the shipped net reaches ~141k on the documented 40-game protocol.
asi.next_action_hint: If the picker's nn2 number is ever challenged, the protocol is documented in docs/solver-history.md ('同梱 net 更新後の表示スコア再測定').

description: Weight-space merge of the two 60k polishes (seed-1 shipped + seed-2 candidate): four-seed sum 569,744.8 vs 584,697.0 (-2.6%), benchmark 151,911.8 (+0.8%, inside noise), while 1-ply rises. Fifth instance of the smoothing signature; docs updated instead.

asi.conclusion: Averaging the two 60k polishes in weight space gives 569,745 across four seeds (vs 584,697 shipped, -2.6%) while 1-ply rises (281,178 vs 271,000): the fifth instance of the 1-ply-up/2-ply-down smoothing signature. Recorded in docs/solver-history.md with all five cases.
asi.hypothesis: Two 60k polishes from the same 30k net differ only by RNG stream, so their weight average may sit in the same basin and combine the strengths (or at least reduce the +/-4% variance).
asi.next_action_hint: Do not merge nets in weight space. The 2-ply objective rewards a sharp V; any averaging operation (SWA, low-lr, symmetry, merge) trades 2-ply for 1-ply.
asi.signature: 1-ply up, 2-ply down; five independent instances now documented.

description: 4-ply only at <=2 empties (phase_h10, new row 27): 12 games seed 9200 = 152,498.7 with 12/12 reaching 8192, but 10.03 ms/move (9.1x the 2-ply baseline) and 8,569 leaves/move. Score gain is inside noise; latency rules it out as the default.

asi.conclusion: The 4-ply endgame converts 12/12 games to 8192 (h6 converted 18/20) but costs 10.03 ms/move native, about 9x the 2-ply baseline, and scores 152,499 (only +1,751, inside noise). Not shippable as the default policy; the tail gain is real-looking but the price is a frame drop on every move.
asi.hypothesis: h6 (3-ply at <=3 empties) bought +12.6k on the benchmark; one more own move and spawn layer at <=2 empties might convert the last 8192 misses.
asi.measured: row 27 (phase_h10): 12 games @9200 = 152,498.7, 12/12 8192, 8,568.6 leaves/move, 10.03 ms/move; 3-game probe 139,798.7 (15.05 ms/move, first-games warmup).
asi.next_action_hint: If the app ever adopts a time budget per move, an endgame-only 4-ply (<=2 empties) is the most promising search option measured (12/12 8192). Until then the depth line is closed: 4-ply everywhere is 21.9x and +2.5%, 3-ply everywhere 12.7x and +8%, endgame 3-ply 4x and a coin flip, endgame 4-ply 9x and +1.2%.
asi.trade_off: 9.1x ms/move for +1.2% score (noise) and a visibly better 8192 rate (12/12 vs 18/20).

description: README/policy_info score refresh on the documented 20+20 protocol: nn2 141,885 (9000 135,419.4 / 9100 148,349.8), nn3 152,463 (157,429.2 / 147,497.2). Corrects the pre-polish 121,569 / 137,342 that the page and README still advertised.

asi.conclusion: Product-facing numbers now match the shipped net on the README's own protocol: nn2 141,885 (9000 135,419.4 / 9100 148,349.8, both 19-20 of 20 reach 8192 after the first run's 16/20), nn3 152,463 (157,429.2 / 147,497.2). README table, policy_info strings and docs agree.
asi.hypothesis: policy_info and the README table still advertised pre-polish numbers (nn2 121,569 / nn3 137,342); the README states a 20+20-game protocol (seeds 9000 and 9100) that had not been re-measured with the shipped net.
asi.next_action_hint: The 9000 half of nn2 is the weak one (16/20 8192); a future net should be checked on both halves before the README number is refreshed again.

description: Polish learning-rate sweep upper point: 60k from the pre-polish 300k net at lr 4e-4 gives a four-seed sum of 563,610 (vs 584,697 at 3e-4) and 142,850.4 on the benchmark. Brackets the polish lr at 3e-4.

asi.conclusion: Polish lr 4e-4 is worse than 3e-4 on every statistic that matters: four-seed sum 563,610 vs 584,697 (-3.6%), benchmark 142,850.4 (-5.2%), 9400 -22,145. The winning polish point is lr 3e-4 for 60k games; 4e-4 is too hot (it does not diverge, it just stops improving).
asi.hypothesis: The 60k polish at lr 3e-4 gained +11% over the 300k net; maybe 4e-4 moves further in the same time.
asi.measured: resume 60k from the exact pre-polish 300k net (sha c98ea27c, recovered via git show 017da7f^) at lr 4e-4, seed 1, par sqrt: 9000 143,142.4, 9200 142,850.4, 9300 146,059.2, 9400 131,557.8; 18-19/20 8192; 1.18-1.38 ms/move.
asi.next_action_hint: The polish lr is bracketed: 3e-4 wins (584,697), 4e-4 loses (563,610), and above that is the base recipe's 3e-3 which needs no polish. Do not re-sweep this range without a new target.

description: Out-of-sample verdict on the #26 candidate: on seeds 9500/9600 (never used for any decision) the seed-2 polish scores 152,174.6 / 147,647.6 vs the shipped 155,944.2 / 151,678.0, losing on both. Its +4.2% was a selection effect; adoption now requires two fresh seeds.

asi.conclusion: Out-of-sample the seed-2 polish loses to the shipped net on both fresh seeds (-3,770 and -4,030), so its +4.2% on 9000-9400 was a selection effect. The #26 discard is now proven rather than argued, and the adoption rule is tightened: a net must win on two seeds it was not selected on.
asi.hypothesis: The seed-2 60k polish only looked +4.2% better because the four comparison seeds were also the selection seeds; fresh seeds 9500/9600 would reveal the selection effect.
asi.measured: seed-2 net on 9500 152,174.6 (19/20) and 9600 147,647.6 (19/20); shipped net on the same 155,944.2 and 151,678.0. Reversal on both fresh seeds.
asi.next_action_hint: Net selection now requires: four-seed screen, then two fresh seeds both >= shipped (docs/measurement.md). Any future polish variant has to clear that bar.

description: Paired verification of the shipped net vs the pre-polish 300k net: pairw 10 games seed 9000 gives diff (B-A) -9,852.0 +/- 13,416.3 with 3/10 wins for B, i.e. the shipped net leads in the right direction; 10 games does not reach the 2-sigma adoption bar. Docs record the tape/absolute-value caveat.

asi.conclusion: The paired instrument confirms the direction (+9,852 for the shipped net) but 10 games is too few for the docs' 2-sigma rule; 20 games would be needed. pairw's absolute scores (155k-176k) are not comparable with the unpaired table because the spawn tape differs even at the same seed.
asi.hypothesis: The docs adopt nets with pairw (A=reference, B=candidate, mean diff minus 2 stderr > 0); the session's +11.8% had never been checked with that instrument.
asi.measured: pairw 10 games seed 9000: diff (B - A) = -9,852.0 +/- 13,416.3, B ahead in 3/10, 510.5 s wall. A=shipped 60k, B=pre-polish 300k.
asi.next_action_hint: For a formal adoption claim, run pairw with 20 games. Note the sign convention: the summary prints B - A, so a negative diff means A (the shipped net) won.

description: Generalization check on two more untouched seeds: shipped net scores 151,499.4 (seed 9700) and 144,591.8 (seed 9800), giving a nine-seed mean of 148,528.9 with no seed below 135k. Baseline is 134,867.2. Docs record the full table.

asi.conclusion: The improvement is not benchmark-specific: no seed falls below 135k, 8192 is reached in 17-19/20 on fresh seeds, and the benchmark seed (9200) sits near the middle of the nine-seed distribution rather than at its top.
asi.hypothesis: If the +11.8% were overfit to seed 9200, held-out seeds would fall back toward 124k; two more untouched seeds (9700, 9800) were evaluated to test that.
asi.next_action_hint: No new training lever above the shipped net is left inside the recipe; remaining candidates are product decisions (per-move time budget for endgame depth) and an optional 20-game pairw for a formal adoption claim.

description: Frozen hidden layer (head-only training, 33 params) for 60k games at lr 1e-2 from the shipped net: 9200 scores 102,012.0 (7/20 8192, 1-ply 44,577.8, 4/20 dead) vs 150,747.2. Freezing the representation and only recalibrating the head destroys 2-ply strength. Code and weights reverted, tree clean.

asi.discrepancy: The earlier freeze sweep in this session was never written to .auto/log.jsonl (no commits, no artifacts survive), so its reported 'frozen head 1.02x sum' could not be reproduced; this logged run is the authoritative measurement and it is a clear loss.
asi.hypothesis: Only 33 parameters (the 32->1 head) need to change to recalibrate V, so a much hotter lr (1e-2, 33x the 3e-4 polish) on a frozen hidden layer might add calibration without moving the representation that 2-ply depends on.
asi.incident: A malformed invocation (`zig build nn -- 60000`, no positional weights path) trained on the default path and wrote ai/solver/nn_weights.bin; restored with git checkout and verified sha bbbff5fe9f7c644c.
asi.measured: Frozen hidden layer, 60k polish from the shipped net at lr 1e-2, par sqrt(8), seed 1: checkpoint at ~55k games (killed at the 25 min tool cap). 9200 20 games = 102,012.0 vs 150,747.2, 8192 7/20 vs 18/20, 1-ply 44,577.8 vs 64,201.4, 4/20 dead below 2048.
asi.next_action_hint: Frozen-head calibration is closed at hot lr. The representation, not the head, carries the 2-ply strength; any further polish needs full-network updates at 3e-4, which is saturated.
asi.rollback_reason: 102,012.0 is -32% against 150,747.2 with fewer 8192 and more dead games.

description: Endgame 3-ply (h6) with the corrected row index: 9200 20 games 148,593.8 (vs 150,747.2) at 3.29 ms/move; seed 9800 paired 20 games gives +3,996.0 +/- 9,395.2 (12W/8L) at 14.40 vs 3.95 ms/move. Five-seed h6 evidence is all under 1.1 sigma for 3.2-3.6x latency: rejected.

asi.conclusion: Endgame 3-ply (h6) is not a win at 3.2-3.6x cost: one seed is clearly positive, three are within noise, and the benchmark seed is slightly negative. Reject it.
asi.hypothesis: The h6 endgame 3-ply mode (2-ply above 3 empties, 3-ply at <=3 with the tight cut) looked like +8% on a single seed; a fresh paired seed (9800) and a re-measured benchmark would settle whether the gain is real.
asi.next_action_hint: Search depth is closed for good: h6 records +12.6k/+10.8k/+0.7k/+2.7k/+4.0k across five seeds, all under 1.1 sigma, at 3.2-3.6x latency. Only a product-level time budget could revive it.
asi.notes: Row indices shifted: after the 4-ply sample rows were added, h4 is row 8, h6 row 9. A pairrow attempt with row 27 accidentally measured the 4-ply spawn-sample row (26-77 ms/move), which is why two runs looked pathologically slow.
asi.rollback_reason: Benchmark 148,593.8 < 150,747.2 and the paired gain on 9800 is 0.4 sigma at 3.6x cost.

description: Formal 20-game paired comparison (A = shipped 60k net, B = pre-polish 300k net from git, sha c98ea27c): mean diff (B-A) = -16,403.2 +/- 13,079.5 with B ahead in only 7/20, confirming the polish gain in direction and magnitude (unpaired: +21,737). Docs note the earlier 10-game run used a wrong B and that a 2-sigma claim needs ~60 games.

asi.conclusion: The polish gain is confirmed in direction and magnitude by the project's paired instrument (+16.4k vs +21.7k unpaired), but a 20-game pairw cannot clear its own 2-sigma bar; adoption stays justified by the nine-seed unpaired table.
asi.hypothesis: The project adopts nets with pairw (A=reference, B=candidate, mean diff - 2 stderr > 0); running it with the true pre-polish net on 20 games would either formalize or refute the session's +19.1% six-seed gain.
asi.measured: pairw 20 games seed 9000: A=shipped 60k, B=pre-polish 300k (sha c98ea27c). mean diff (B-A) = -16,403.2 +/- 13,079.5, B ahead in 7/20, 902.5 s.
asi.next_action_hint: A formal 2-sigma claim would need ~60 paired games; not worth the compute. The nine-seed unpaired table is the stronger evidence.

description: Third independent 60k polish sample (train seed 3): 9000 121,742.0 / 9200 139,297.2 / 9300 142,744.2 / 9400 147,059.2, four-seed sum 550,842.6 vs the shipped 584,697.0 (-5.8%). With three samples (584.7k, 609.4k, 550.8k) the polish's seed sd is +-5%, and the shipped net is near the mean: the recipe has no headroom left. Base 300k reproduced bit-identically again (sha c98ea27c).

asi.conclusion: The polish has no headroom left: its train-seed spread is +-5%, the shipped net sits at the sample mean, and picking the best of several polishes is selection bias that does not survive fresh seeds (consistent with the seed-2 candidate failing on 9500/9600).
asi.hypothesis: The 60k polish is trajectory dependent (seed 2 gave +4.2% on four seeds), so a third independent polish sample (train seed 3) was run to measure the distribution and check for real headroom above the shipped net.
asi.next_action_hint: Nothing measurable is left in this architecture/recipe: EXPSPAWN, depth, freeze, merge, lr, schedules, targets are all closed with numbers. Any further score gain needs a different representation (CNN/residual, format change) or a product time budget.
asi.notes: The base 300k recipe reproduced bit-identically again (553,202,634 moves, sha c98ea27c), so all remaining variance is seed choice, not run noise.

description: Capacity axis closed: h1=160 with the identical recipe (300k base + 60k polish) scores 86,881.8 / 93,070.8 / 89,585.2 / 92,080.4 = 361,618.2 (-38% vs the shipped 584,697.0), 8192 19/80. The wider layer is badly calibrated at the same lr/batch_scale. Also confirmed the p2 (2-ply self-play) fine-tune is cost-closed at ~3.6 s/game.

asi.conclusion: Capacity is closed at h1=128: 96, 160, 192 and 256 all lose, 160 by -38%. The wider layer needs more gradient steps at the same lr/batch_scale, and its V ends up uncorrelated with 2-ply strength (self-play 78k, 2-ply 93k). p2 fine-tuning was also cost-closed: 2-ply self-play is ~3.6 s/game, so the 5,000-game minimum checkpoint is 5 h.
asi.hypothesis: The last untested capacity point (h1=160 with the identical recipe) might beat 128; if not, the capacity axis closes and the recipe is at its ceiling.
asi.next_action_hint: No measurable lever remains without changing the representation (CNN/residual, weight-format change, full retrain) or a product time budget. Recommend stopping the optimization loop and reporting the result.
asi.p2_cost: p2 variant (2-ply self-play) ran 6+ min without finishing 100 games (par, 8 threads) and wrote no checkpoint; the smallest useful fine-tune (5,000 games) is ~5 h.
asi.type: capacity point h1=160 with the full recipe
